sara_sales: Quick sync — BrightLoop POC scoping. Customer wants a fraud-detection assistant POC. Need alignment on success criteria, auth requirements, rate limits, streaming vs polling, and timeline. Can eng confirm SDK options and recommended auth for an enterprise trial? cc @dan_engineer @elaine_pse @tom_se

dan_engineer: We can support Node/Python SDKs. For realtime streams: hosted supports chunked HTTP (SSE) and streaming via chunked responses; Dedicated offers gRPC streaming if they want persistent connections. If sub-200ms p50 is a hard requirement, recommend Dedicated or Private with websocket/gRPC.

elaine_pse: Proposal for success criteria: 1) evaluation dataset of ~500 labelled prompts, 2) top-1 precision >= 94% on fraud classification prompts, 3) avg token cost <= $0.015 per query during POC, 4) p50 latency < 150ms for typical prompt sizes. Timebox: 3 weeks (wk1 integration + auth, wk2 run evals & tuning, wk3 quality verification + handoff). Thoughts?

tom_se: For auth: customer requires SAML SSO + audit logs. For the POC we should do a scoped API key + IP allowlist to move fast. If they want SSO integration, we can plug into their Okta and create a service account; that adds ~1 week for SAML config and testing. For Private we can offer mTLS as well.

jen_cust_success: I'll run the POC runbook and daily standups. FYI default hosted quota is 60 req/s and token window limits apply. We can request a temporary bump for the trial — size depends on expected concurrency. Also ask them for a representative prompt set (500) and traffic pattern (rps peaks).

dan_engineer: Implementation notes — retries and idempotency: our generate endpoint is not strictly idempotent. Recommend client generate a request_id header and do retry on 5xx with exponential backoff (max 3 retries). We'll provide sample snippet: ```javascript
// idempotent-ish retry example
const resp = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'X-Request-Id': reqId },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});
// backoff on 500/502/503
```

tom_se: For streaming clients: include a reconnect strategy that resumes by re-sending last_token_index or prompt prefix. If they can't use streaming, chunked HTTP is fine but increases latency. Also note: client-side prefix caching helps for repeated context across queries.

jen_cust_success: Security Qs from BrightLoop: data residency controls, log retention, and whether customer data is used for training. Short answers: hosted — data can be isolated per-tenant for enterprise (we do not train on PII by default; we have contractual controls). I'll send the formal security questionnaire after this thread.

dan_engineer: Action items for eng: 1) provide Node+Python sample for streaming + non-streaming (due EOD tomorrow), 2) sample retry/idempotency code (tomorrow), 3) guidance on request headers and rate-limit headers (we expose X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining).

jen_cust_success: Action items for sales/CS: 1) collect 500 eval prompts and traffic profile from BrightLoop by Tue, 2) request hosted quota bump (filed), 3) schedule kickoff call for Monday.

deploy-bot: Quota request submitted: Q-223 (pending infra approval) :rocket:

sara_sales: Perfect. I'll coordinate with BrightLoop for the prompt pack and push the kickoff. If eng posts samples here I'll loop them in. Thanks all :thumbsup:

elaine_pse: One more note — let's include an A/B test in week3: baseline model vs a tuned prompt/template. If we hit the success criteria we suggest extending to Dedicated for sustained low-latency.

dan_engineer: ACK. I'll drop the code samples and a short integration checklist (auth, SDK snippet, headers to watch) in this thread by EOD.

sara_sales: Great — closing the loop here. Meeting invite once Jen confirms Wed/Tue from the customer.
